title: Chapter 7. Praise of Nitai and Chaitanya, the Appearance of Nityananda and Gaura, Nimai's Childhood, the Abhisheka, Kirtanas, the Sannyasa, Nilachala, the Deities at Ambika, Prayers
html:
Padas of contemporaries known from the Padakalpataru (PK), in the order of the lilas: praise of Nitai and Chaitanya and of the sankirtana (Krishnadasa); Nityananda's appearance at Ekachakra (Krishnadasa); Gaura's appearance and His childhood play in Shachi's house (Vasu Ghosha); the Govardhana of bhakti in Navadvipa (Chaitanyadasa); the abhisheka in Srivasa's house (Krishnadasa); the dance of the Lord hearing of Vrindavana (Ramachandra); Nityananda's dance (Vasu Ramananda); separation in autumn (Krishnadasa); the sannyasi Lord on the seashore (Ramananda); Nilachala (Paramananda); the Deities of Gaura and Nitai in Gauridasa's house at Ambika (Krishnadasa); and Krishnadasa's prayers. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the variants of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) and the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Krishnadasa — "prema-sindhu gorā rāy…" (PK 2343)

Praise of Nitai and Chaitanya: Gaura is an ocean of prema, Nitai the wave upon it; Rupa and Sanatana, diving into this ocean, bring up jewels and string them on the thread of bhakti; the kirtana of the lilas is a blossoming lotus forest. In PK it stands in the 23rd pallava (the form and qualities of Chaitanya and Nityananda). Raga dhanashi.1

প্রেম-সিন্ধু গোরা রায় নিতাই-তরঙ্গ তায়
করুণা-বাতাস চারি পাশে ।
প্রেম উথলিয়া পড়ে জগত হাফান ছাড়ে
তাপ তৃষ্ণা সভাকার নাশে ॥

prema-sindhu gorā rāya nitāi-taraṅga tāya
karuṇā-bātāsa cāri pāśe |
prema uthaliyā paṛe jagata hāphāna chāṛe
tāpa tṛṣṇā sabhākāra nāśe ||

prema-sindhu — the ocean of prema; gorā rāy — Gora Raya; nitāi-taraṅga tāy — Nitai the wave upon it; karuṇā-bātāsa — the wind of compassion; cāri pāśe — on all four sides; prema uthaliyā paṛe — prema surges and spills over; jagata hāphān chāṛe — the world draws breath (sighs with relief); tāpa tṛṣṇā — heat and thirst; sabhākāra nāśe — are destroyed for all

1.1An ocean of prema is Gora Raya, Nitai the wave upon it,
on all four sides — the wind of compassion.
Prema surges and spills over — the world draws breath again:
everyone's heat and thirst are gone.2

দেখ দেখ নিতাই চৈতন্য দয়াময় ।
ভক্ত-হংস-চক্রবাকে পিব পিব বলি ডাকে
পাইয়া বঞ্চিত কেন হয় ॥ ধ্রু ॥

dekha dekha nitāi caitanya dayāmaya |
bhakta-haṃsa-cakrabāke piba piba bali ḍāke
pāiyā bañcita kena haya || dhru ||

dekha dekha — behold, behold; nitāi caitanya dayāmaya — the merciful Nitai and Chaitanya; bhakta-haṃsa-cakrabāke — the swans and chakravakas, the devotees; piba piba bali ḍāke — call, saying "Drink, drink!"; pāiyā — having found; bañcita kena haya — why does one stay deprived

1.2(Refrain) Behold, behold the merciful Nitai and Chaitanya!
To the swans and chakravakas — the devotees — They call: "Drink, drink!"
Having found such a thing, why stay deprived?3

ডুবি রূপ সনাতন তোলে নানা রত্ন ধন
যতনে গাঁথিয়া তার মালা ।
ভক্তি-লতা-সূত্র করি লেহ জীব কণ্ঠ ভরি
দূরে যাবে তপনের জ্বালা ॥

ḍubi rūpa sanātana tole nānā ratna dhana
yatane gām̐thiyā tāra mālā |
bhakti-latā-sūtra kari leha jība kaṇṭha bhari
dūre yābe tapanera jvālā ||

ḍubi — diving; rūpa sanātana — Rupa and Sanatana; tole nānā ratna dhana — bring up many jewel-treasures; yatane gāṃthiyā tāra mālā — carefully stringing a garland of them; bhakti-latā-sūtra kari — making the creeper of bhakti the thread; leha jība — take it, souls; kaṇṭha bhari — filling (adorning) the neck; dūre yābe tapanera jvālā — the burning of the sun will go away

1.3Diving, Rupa and Sanatana bring up many treasures, jewels,
and carefully string a garland of them.
Making the creeper of bhakti the thread — take it, souls, adorn your necks:
the scorching heat of the sun will go.4

লীলা-রস সংকীর্ত্তন বিকসিত পদ্ম-বন
জগত ভরিল যার বাসে ।
ফুটিল কুসুম বন মাতিল ভ্রমরগণ
পাইয়া বঞ্চিত কৃষ্ণদাসে ॥

līlā-rasa saṃkīrttana bikasita padma-bana
jagata bharila yāra bāse |
phuṭila kusuma bana mātila bhramaragaṇa
pāiyā bañcita kṛṣṇadāse ||

līlā-rasa saṅkīrtana — the sankirtana of the taste of the lilas; bikasita padma-bana — a blossoming lotus forest; jagata bharila — the world was filled; yāra bāse — with whose fragrance; phuṭila kusuma bana — the flower forest bloomed; mātila bhramara-gaṇa — the bees became intoxicated; pāiyā — having found; bañcita kṛṣṇadāse — Krishnadasa is deprived

1.4The sankirtana of the taste of the lilas is a blossoming lotus forest,
whose fragrance has filled the world.
The forest of flowers has bloomed, the bees are intoxicated —
yet Krishnadasa, having found it, has stayed deprived.5

dhanashi; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2447. GPT1 — pp. 32–33, no. 19 (raga dhanashi); GPT2 — sect. 1.3, no. 19. Which Krishnadasa wrote the pada is not established: PK gathers under this signature padas of different poets (including Krishnadasa Kaviraja); the mention of Rupa and Sanatana dates it not earlier than 1514–1516. Majumdar does not discuss it. "ka" and GPT1 — hākāla ("the world cries out"). Ms. "kha": "sin" (pāpa) instead of "heat". thread of a book" (grantha) instead of "creeper". "The heat of the sun" is worldly suffering; GPT1: "your burning will go".

2. Krishnadasa — "nabadvīpe śuni siṃhanāda…" (PK 2089)

The sankirtana in Navadvipa as a battle: Gaurachandra is the great chariot-warrior, Nityananda the general, Advaita the vanguard; the enemies are bound with a noose of the rope of prema; the Lord, mounted on the elephant of Kali, sets up outposts on every side. In PK it stands in the 17th pallava (the dance and pastimes of Gauranga). Raga ramakeli.6

নবদ্বীপে শুনি সিংহনাদ ।
সাজল বৈষ্ণবগণ করি হরি সংকীর্ত্তন
মূঢ়মতি গণিল প্রমাদ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nabadvīpe śuni siṃhanāda |
sājala baiṣṇabagaṇa kari hari saṃkīrttana
mūṛhamati gaṇila pramāda || dhru ||

nabadvīpe — in Navadvipa; śuni — is heard; siṃhanāda — a lion's roar; sājala baiṣṇaba-gaṇa — the Vaishnavas arrayed themselves; kari hari saṅkīrtana — performing the sankirtana of Hari; mūṛhamati — the fools; gaṇila pramāda — reckoned it a calamity

2.1(Refrain) In Navadvipa a lion's roar was heard!
The Vaishnavas arrayed themselves, starting the sankirtana of Hari —
the fools took it for a calamity.7

গৌরচন্দ্র মহারথী নিত্যানন্দ সেনাপতি
অদ্বৈত যুদ্ধের আগুয়ান ।
প্রেম-ডোর ফাঁস করি বান্ধিল অনেক ঐরি
নিরন্তর গর্জ্জে হরিনাম ॥

gauracandra mahārathī nityānanda senāpati
advaita yuddhera āguyāna |
prema-ḍora phām̐sa kari bāndhila aneka airi
nirantara garjje harināma ||

gauracandra mahārathī — Gaurachandra the great chariot-warrior; nityānanda senāpati — Nityananda the general; advaita yuddhera āguyāna — Advaita the vanguard of the battle; prema-ḍora phāṃsa kari — making a noose of the rope of prema; bāndhila aneka airi — they bound many foes; nirantara garjje hari-nāma — unceasingly thunders the name of Hari

2.2Gaurachandra is the great chariot-warrior, Nityananda the general,
Advaita at the head of the army.
With a noose of the rope of prema they bound many foes;
unceasingly thunders the name of Hari.

শ্রীচৈতন্য করে রণ কলি-গজে আরোহণ
পাষণ্ড-দলন বীর-বানা ।
কলি-জীব তরাইতে আইল প্রভু অবনীতে
চৌদিকে চাপিয়া দিল থানা ॥

śrīcaitanya kare raṇa kali-gaje ārohaṇa
pāṣaṇḍa-dalana bīra-bānā |
kali-jība tarāite āila prabhu abanīte
caudike cāpiyā dila thānā ||

śrīcaitanya kare raṇa — Sri Chaitanya wages battle; kali-gaje ārohaṇa — mounted on the elephant of Kali; pāṣaṇḍa-dalana — the crusher of godlessness; bīra-bānā — [in] the array of a hero; kali-jība tarāite — to deliver the souls of the Kali age; āila prabhu abanīte — the Lord came to the earth; caudike cāpiyā dila thānā — set up outposts all around

2.3Sri Chaitanya wages the battle, mounted on the elephant of Kali,
in the array of a hero, the crusher of godlessness.
To deliver the souls of the Kali age the Lord came to the earth
and set up outposts on all four sides.8

উত্তম অধম জন সভে পাইল প্রেম-ধন
নিতাই-চৈতন্য-কৃপা-লেশে ।
সমুখে শমন দেখি কৃষ্ণদাস বড় দুখী
না পাইয়া প্রেমের উদ্দেশে ॥

uttama adhama jana sabhe pāila prema-dhana
nitāi-caitanya-kṛpā-leśe |
samukhe śamana dekhi kṛṣṇadāsa baṛa dukhī
nā pāiyā premera uddeśe ||

uttama adhama jana — high and low people; sabhe pāila prema-dhana — all obtained the treasure of prema; nitāi-caitanya-kṛpā-leśe — by a particle of the mercy of Nitai and Chaitanya; samukhe śamana dekhi — seeing Yama before him; kṛṣṇadāsa baṛa dukhī — Krishnadasa is very sorrowful; nā pāiyā premera uddeśe — not having found a trace of prema

2.4High and low — all obtained the treasure of prema
by a particle of the mercy of Nitai and Chaitanya.
But Krishnadasa, seeing Yama before him, grieves deeply:
he has not found even a trace of prema.9

ramakeli; ms. P-R-Sa no. 2198; after the pada a PK rubric: here the pada "kali timira ghora…" is also sung. GPT1 — p. 274, no. 85 (raga ramakeli); GPT2 — sect. 4.2. The catalogue's former first line ("kali-jība tarāite…") is the beginning of the third stanza. Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established. (cf. CB Madhya 23). mss. "ka", "kha", "ca": "mounted on an elephant" (kari-gaje). GPT1: "Nityananda is the charioteer" (sārathi) instead of "the general". The Lord crushes godlessness (pāṣaṇḍa) not with weapons but with the holy name: cf. CC Adi 17 — the Kazi subdued by the kirtana.

3. Krishnadasa — "jaya jaya mahāprabhu jaya gauracandra…" (PK 2847)

A nama-kirtana: glory to Mahaprabhu, His parents, Navadvipa, the Ganga, the Lord's consorts and His devotees. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the morning lila (32nd pallava, the "eightfold lila"). Raga "kau".10

জয় জয় মহাপ্রভু জয় গৌরচন্দ্র ।
জয় বিশ্বম্ভর জয় করুণার সিন্ধু ॥

jaya jaya mahāprabhu jaya gauracandra |
jaya biśvambhara jaya karuṇāra sindhu ||

jaya jaya mahāprabhu — glory, glory to Mahaprabhu; jaya gauracandra — glory to Gaurachandra; jaya biśvambhara — glory to Vishvambhara; jaya karuṇāra sindhu — glory to the ocean of mercy

3.1Glory, glory to Mahaprabhu, glory to Gaurachandra!
Glory to Vishvambhara, glory to the ocean of mercy!

জয় শচীসুত জয় পণ্ডিত নিমাঞি ।
জয় মিশ্র পুরন্দর জয় শচী আই ॥

jaya śacīsuta jaya paṇḍita nimāñi |
jaya miśra purandara jaya śacī āi ||

jaya śacīsuta — glory to the Son of Shachi; jaya paṇḍita nimāñi — glory to Pandita Nimai; jaya miśra purandara — glory to Mishra Purandara; jaya śacī āi — glory to Mother Shachi

3.2Glory to the Son of Shachi, glory to Pandita Nimai!
Glory to Mishra Purandara, glory to Mother Shachi!

জয় জয় নবদ্বীপ জয় সুরধুনী ।
জয় লক্ষ্মী বিষ্ণুপ্রিয়া প্রভুর গৃহিণী ॥

jaya jaya nabadvīpa jaya suradhunī |
jaya lakṣmī biṣṇupriyā prabhura gṛhiṇī ||

jaya jaya nabadvīpa — glory, glory to Navadvipa; jaya suradhunī — glory to the Suradhuni (the Ganga); jaya lakṣmī biṣṇupriyā — glory to Lakshmi and Vishnupriya; prabhura gṛhiṇī — the Lord's consorts

3.3Glory, glory to Navadvipa, glory to the Suradhuni!
Glory to Lakshmi and Vishnupriya, the Lord's consorts!11

জয় জয় নবদ্বীপ-বাসী ভক্তগণ ।
জয় জয় নিত্যানন্দ অদ্বৈত-চরণ ॥

jaya jaya nabadvīpa-bāsī bhaktagaṇa |
jaya jaya nityānanda advaita-caraṇa ||

jaya jaya nabadvīpa-bāsī bhakta-gaṇa — glory, glory to the devotees dwelling in Navadvipa; jaya jaya nityānanda advaita-caraṇa — glory, glory to the feet of Nityananda and Advaita

3.4Glory, glory to the devotees who dwell in Navadvipa!
Glory, glory to the feet of Nityananda and Advaita!

নিত্যানন্দ-পদ-দ্বন্দ্ব সদা করি আশ ।
নাম-সংকীর্ত্তন গাইল কৃষ্ণদাস ॥

nityānanda-pada-dvandva sadā kari āśa |
nāma-saṃkīrttana gāila kṛṣṇadāsa ||

nityānanda-pada-dvandva — the two feet of Nityananda; sadā kari āśa — ever hoping [for]; nāma-saṅkīrtana — the nama-sankirtana; gāila kṛṣṇadāsa — Krishnadasa sang

3.5Ever hoping for the two feet of Nityananda,
Krishnadasa has sung this nama-sankirtana.12

lila. Sri Gaurachandra", no. 10 (mark "॥১০॥২৮৪৭॥"); raga "kau" (an abbreviation; so also GPT1). GPT1 — pp. 22–23, no. 62 (without couplet 3.3); GPT2 — sect. 1.2, no. 62. The attribution is not established; the hope placed in Nityananda's feet in the signature points rather to a poet of Nityananda's branch than to Krishnadasa Kaviraja. Lord's first consort; Vishnupriya the second.

4. Krishnadasa — "rāṛhadeśe nāma ekacakrā grāma…" (PK 1116)

Nityananda's appearance: in Radha-desha, in the village of Ekachakra, in the house of Hadai Pandita, on the bright thirteenth of Magha, Haladhara was born; Hadai celebrates his son's birth, the earth sways with joy; Advaita in Shantipura perceives that Rama, Krishna's elder brother, has appeared. In PK: "Then the appearance of Shri Nityananda-chandra" (3rd shakha, 18th pallava, the "janma-lila"). Raga shri.13

রাঢ়দেশে নাম একচক্রা গ্রাম
হাড়াই পণ্ডিত-ঘর ।
শুভ মাঘ-মাসি শুক্লা ত্রয়োদশী
জনমিলা হলধর ॥

rāṛhadeśe nāma ekacakrā grāma
hāṛāi paṇḍita-ghara |
śubha māgha-māsi śuklā trayodaśī
janamilā haladhara ||

rāṛhadeśe — in Radha-desha; nāma ekacakrā grāma — the village named Ekachakra; hāṛāi paṇḍita-ghara — the house of Hadai Pandita; śubha māgha-māsi — in the auspicious month of Magha; śuklā trayodaśī — on the bright thirteenth; janamilā haladhara — Haladhara (Balarama) was born

4.1In Radha-desha, in the village named Ekachakra,
in the house of Hadai Pandita,
in the auspicious month of Magha, on the bright thirteenth,
Haladhara was born.14

হাড়াই পণ্ডিত অতি হরষিত
পুত্র-মহোৎসব করে ।
ধরণী-মণ্ডল করে টলমল
আনন্দ নাহিক ধরে ॥

hāṛāi paṇḍita ati haraṣita
putra-mahotsaba kare |
dharaṇī-maṇḍala kare ṭalamala
ānanda nāhika dhare ||

hāṛāi paṇḍita — Hadai Pandita; ati haraṣita — overjoyed; putra-mahotsaba kare — holds a festival for his son; dharaṇī-maṇḍala — the circle of the earth; kare ṭalamala — sways; ānanda nāhika dhare — cannot contain the bliss

4.2Hadai Pandita, filled with joy,
holds a festival for his son.
The circle of the earth sways,
unable to contain the bliss.

শান্তিপুর-নাথ মনে হরষিত
করি কিছু অনুমান ।
অন্তরে জানিলা বুঝি জনমিলা
কৃষ্ণের অগ্রজ রাম ॥

śāntipura-nātha mane haraṣita
kari kichu anumāna |
antare jānilā bujhi janamilā
kṛṣṇera agraja rāma ||

śāntipura-nātha — the Lord of Shantipura (Advaita); mane haraṣita — rejoicing at heart; kari kichu anumāna — divining something; antare jānilā — He knew within; bujhi janamilā — surely there is born; kṛṣṇera agraja rāma — Rama, Krishna's elder brother

4.3The Lord of Shantipura, rejoicing,
divined something:
in His heart He knew: surely there is born
Rama, the elder brother of Krishna.15

বৈষ্ণবের মন হৈল পরসন্ন
আনন্দ-সাগরে ভাসে ।
এ দীন পামর হইবে উদ্ধার
কহে দুখী কৃষ্ণদাসে ॥

baiṣṇabera mana haila parasanna
ānanda-sāgare bhāse |
e dīna pāmara haibe uddhāra
kahe dukhī kṛṣṇadāse ||

baiṣṇabera mana — the hearts of the Vaishnavas; haila parasanna — became serene; ānanda-sāgare bhāse — float in an ocean of bliss; e dīna pāmara — this wretched sinner; haibe uddhāra — will be delivered; kahe dukhī kṛṣṇadāse — says the unhappy Krishnadasa

4.4The hearts of the Vaishnavas grew serene,
they float in an ocean of bliss.
"Even this wretched sinner will be delivered,"
says the unhappy Krishnadasa.16

section "tataḥ śrīnityānandacandrābirbhābaḥ", no. 5 (mark "॥৫॥১১১৬॥"); raga shri; ms. P-R-Sa no. 1614. GPT1 — p. 416, no. 7 (raga shri); GPT2 — sect. 6.1, no. 7. In the catalogue the pada was listed as PK 1117 (PK 1117 is the next pada, below, no. 5). Which Krishnadasa it is has not been established. ("bearer of the plough") is Balarama: Nityananda is Balarama Himself. Magha is January–February; the same date is in the Advaita-prakasha. Ms. "ka" and P-R-Sa: "Radha-desh" (without the locative ending).

5. Krishnadasa — "bhubana-ānanda-kanda balarāma nityānanda…" (PK 1117)

Praise of Nityananda, descended in the Kali age: He is golden like the champaka, the nails of His fingers are a row of moons, His face eclipses the full moon, His arms reach His knees; bee-devotees hover at His lotus feet. In PK it is the next pada of the same section. Raga suhai.17

ভুবন-আনন্দ-কন্দ বলরাম নিত্যানন্দ
অবতীর্ণ হৈলা কলি-কালে ।
ঘুচিল সকল দুখ দেখিয়া ও চান্দমুখ
ভাসে লোক আনন্দ-হিলোলে ॥

12. Chaitanyadasa — "dekha dekha aparūpa gaurāṅga-bilāsa…" (PK 1242)

An allegory: in Navadvipa Gauranga again manifests the lila of lifting Govardhana.
